title: Week 8: Final project, what actually makes deep RL work?

segments.text: Week 8, final project, what actually makes Deep RL work.
Question. Which design choices matter for value-based and policy-based Deep RL,
and how sensitive are they to hyperparameters and random seeds?
Setup.
Environments, Cart Bowl V1, the main test bed, discrete, 4-dim state, solved at 475 plus,
Lunar Lander V3, 8-dim state, 4 actions, solved at greater than or equal to 200,
Pendulum V1, continuous action. Every configuration is trained with three seeds.
Results report training return, last 20 episodes, and greedy evaluation over 20 fresh episodes,
as mean plus or minus STD experiments script one DQN component ablation,
no replay slash no target network slash double DQN run deep.py ablation to DQN hyperparameter
sensitivity, epsilon decay length, batch size, target update period run deep.py DQN tuning
three reinforce with VS without a learned baseline, plus gradient variance measurement run deep.py
reinforce, PG variance.py for value-based VS policy-based.
On Cart Bowl, DQN, reinforce, A2C, PPO run deep.py Cart Bowl V scaling up,
reinforce VS A2C, VS PPO on Lunar Lander, DDPG on pendulum run deep.py lunar.pg pendulum
all tables and figures are in the main readme. Observations and failure cases,
removing the target network does not just slow learning, it diverges. Q values grew by about
five orders of magnitude above their theoretical bound. The plus or minus columns are large for
DQN and A2C, seed variance is often larger than the effect of a hyperparameter.
Reporting a single run would be misleading. PPO was the most robust default algorithm,
solving Cart Bowl and Lunar Lander on every seed without tuning.
Reinforce can reach a perfect greedy policy while its training curve still oscillates,
because the policy keeps being kicked by high variance updates.
Limitations, only three seeds and small compute budgets, CPU, so confidence intervals are wide.
One at a time hyperparameter sweeps misinteractions between settings.
Same network sizes everywhere, with no tuning per algorithm beyond standard defaults.
